text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.
- The Norwegian Labour Directorate plans to recruit 300 doctors every year for the next three years primarily from Germany, Austria and Finland. There is a shortage of doctors in Norway.

- Big Norwegian banks are losing money because it is more beneficial for foreign investors to trade in Norwegian crowns through foreign banks. The Norwegian Banking Association now demands the rules be changed to ensure equal competition.

- The Norwegian defence ministry wants nearly one million crowns in compensation from Canadian anti-whaling activist Paul Watson, who is accused of letting his ship ram a coast guard vessel in Norwegian waters in 1994. The Sea Shepherd leader is in Dutch custody awaiting possible extradition to Norway to serve a 120 day prison term for opening the flood valves of a Norwegian whaling ship in 1992.

- Norwegian salmon farms stand to lose more than 200 annual job equivalents should the EU slap anti-dumping duties on imports of farmed Norwegian salmon. But consumers in the EU will also be affected by such a measure.
- National Planning Minister Bendik Rugaas is giving Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland and other top government leaders hefty pay rises.
- Investor Kjell Inge Roekke is vacuum-cleaning the market for shares in insurance company Storebrand, which is to merge with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse under a proposal presented last week.

- Almost 15 percent of the shares in Fokus Bank have changed hands in the past five trading session on the Oslo stock exchange. At the same time the price has gone up and takeover rumours are plenty. There is reason to believe that the Fokus leadership is mobilising its friends among shareholders in its attempt to buy mortgage lender BNbank.
